source_text: Et ideo super hoc laborandum non est; commendo tamen disputatoris acrimoniam, qui quam dicit a Deo redditam, non vult a Deo conditam; pronuntians Dei non convenire operibus, quod vult eius convenire iudiciis.
pass_a_gloss: And therefore one must not labor upon this; I commend nevertheless the disputant's sharpness, who what he says was rendered by God, he does not want founded by God; pronouncing that what he wants to suit God's judgments does not suit God's works.

lemmas.lexica: LS opus; Blaise God's works vs devil's

pass_b_english: There is therefore no need to labor over this. Still, I commend the disputant’s sharpness: what he says was imposed by God as punishment, he refuses to say was created by God. He pronounces incompatible with God’s works what he wants to be compatible with God’s judgments.

choices.why: Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
Keep Julian's good-of-nature vs good-of-will contrast; do not baptize as 'grace'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
